ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a 555 timer monostable circuit. Pin 8 of the 555 is connected to VCC, and the reset terminal pin 4 is also connected to a high level; pin 1 is grounded; pin 3 is the output vo; pin 5 is connected to ground through a 0.01 μF capacitor; the external resistor R and capacitor C form the timing network. Reasoning: This circuit is a standard 555 monostable trigger, and the output high-level duration is equal to the time required for the timing capacitor to charge through R to 2/3 VCC. The capacitor charging relation is vc = VCC(1 - e^{-t/RC}); setting vc = 2VCC/3 gives e^{-t/RC} = 1/3, therefore t = RC ln 3 ≈ 1.1RC. So the output pulse width is t_w = 1.1RC.

Apply the standard monostable 555 timing relation, where the output remains high while the timing capacitor charges through R up to 2/3 VCC. Therefore t_w = RC ln 3 ≈ 1.1RC.
